harmonicFunction: B5 (i) - Tonic power chord establishing the heavy minor key foundation
D5 (III) - Mediant creating an ascending motion from the tonic
E5 (IV) - Subdominant continuing the ascending power chord movement
G5 (VI) - Submediant providing the upper anchor in the oscillating riff figure
F#5 (V) - Dominant creating tension in the back-and-forth with G5
The riff's ascending B5-D5-E5 opening creates a powerful sense of forward momentum
The G5-F#5-G5 oscillation adds a hypnotic rhythmic quality to the riff

techniques.name: Sliding Power Chords
techniques.description: The defining technique of Iron Man - power chords that slide between positions on the fretboard, creating the iconic heavy riff with smooth glissando transitions rather than lifting and repositioning fingers

notes: B5: X-2-4-4-X-X (2nd fret A string root)
D5: X-5-7-7-X-X (5th fret A string root)
E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (Open low E string root) or X-7-9-9-X-X
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (3rd fret low E string root)
F#5: 2-4-4-X-X-X (2nd fret low E string root)
Slide between chord positions rather than lifting fingers off the fretboard
Maintain consistent fretting pressure during slides for clean transitions
The slow intro uses exaggerated slides for dramatic effect
sequence: Start with B5 power chord shape at 2nd fret A string
Slide up to D5 at 5th fret, then to E5 at 7th fret
Shift to G5 on the low E string at 3rd fret
Oscillate between G5 and F#5 with quick half-step slides
Return to D5 and E5 to complete the riff cycle
tips: Practice the slide motion slowly to maintain clean power chord voicings
Keep your fretting hand in the power chord shape throughout the slides
Apply moderate palm muting for tightness during the main riff sections
The intro slides should be slow and deliberate - heavier is better
details.progression: B5 - D5 - E5 - G5 - F#5 - G5 - F#5 - G5 - D5 - E5 (Main Riff)

techniques.name: Palm Muted Groove
techniques.description: Heavy palm muting applied to the main riff and verse sections, creating the thick, chugging sound that gives Iron Man its ominous, stomping feel

notes: Rest palm edge on the bridge to dampen strings slightly
The muting should be moderate - heavy enough for chug but not dead muting
Combine with downstrokes exclusively for maximum heaviness
Release muting briefly on chord changes for the slide transitions
sequence: Apply palm muting on the B5 chord for the opening chug
Briefly release muting during power chord slides for clean transitions
Re-apply muting when landing on each new chord position
During the G5-F#5 oscillation, maintain consistent muting pressure
tips: The goal is a thick, chunky sound - not completely muted
Practice the muting at slow tempo to find the sweet spot of pressure
The muting pressure should stay consistent through tempo changes
Listen to the original recording for the exact balance of mute vs. sustain
details.progression: Palm muted B5 - D5 - E5 chugging pattern

techniques.name: Pentatonic Soloing with Vibrato
techniques.description: Tony Iommi's lead guitar work over the riff progression, using B minor pentatonic with wide vibrato and expressive bends that define the classic Sabbath lead sound

notes: Based in the 7th and 12th fret B minor pentatonic box positions
Features whole-step bends on the B and G strings for expressive peaks
Wide, slow vibrato is the defining Iommi lead characteristic
Combination of picked notes and legato hammer-on/pull-off phrases
sequence: Open phrases in the 7th fret B minor pentatonic position
Shift up to the 12th fret position for higher intensity moments
Apply whole-step bends with vibrato on sustained notes
Use hammer-on/pull-off runs to connect scale positions
tips: Iommi's vibrato is slow and wide - practice controlled vibrato motion
Bend to pitch accurately - use a tuner to check your bends
The solo should feel heavy and deliberate, not fast or flashy
Study Iommi's unique fingering approach (he lost fingertips and used prosthetics)
details.progression: B minor pentatonic over B5 - D5 - E5 - G5 - F#5

sections.name: Intro (Slow)
sections.description: Tony Iommi's chilling slow entrance, hitting a sustained B5 power chord followed by ominous behind-the-nut string bends
notes: Hold the heavy 7th-fret B5 power chord for full measure sustains
Keep distortion saturated and sustain singing
Let the space between strikes build anticipation
Establishes the crushing slow tempo at 74 BPM

sections.name: Main Riff / Verse
sections.description: The definitive heavy metal guitar riff, shifting from B5 up to D5 and E5 before executing a ferocious chromatic slide between G5 and F#5
sections.progression: B5 | D5 D5 | E5 E5 | G5 F#5 G5 F#5 G5 D5 E5
notes: Strike whole-note B5, then slide up to 10th fret for two punchy D5 chords
Slide to 12th fret for two E5 chords
Execute rapid chromatic slides between 15th fret (G5) and 14th fret (F#5)
Drop back to D5 and resolve on E5 with heavy vibrato

sections.name: Bridge / Fast Section
sections.description: Driving up-tempo groove pushing the song forward into the breakdown
notes: Downstroke power chords locking with Bill Ward's syncopated drumming
Clean hand shifts along the neck
Tight right-hand palm muting for punchy attack
Keep momentum driving steadily

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Tony Iommi's multi-tracked lead solo featuring blistering pentatonic runs, wah-wah sweeps, and double-tracked unison bends
notes: Full 2-octave B minor pentatonic scale run centered around the 7th-fret box
Notes: B, D, E, F#, A moving across all six strings

beginner.title: Getting Started with Iron Man
steps: Learn the B5, D5, E5, G5, and F#5 power chord shapes
Practice sliding between power chord positions slowly
Work on the basic B5-D5-E5 ascending pattern
Build familiarity with the slow intro slides

intermediate.title: Building the Full Riff
steps: Master the complete main riff including the G5-F#5 oscillation
Add palm muting to the riff for authentic heaviness
Learn the bridge section with faster chord changes
Practice at increasing tempos from 100 BPM to 164 BPM

advanced.title: Solo Mastery and Complete Performance
steps: Learn the guitar solo using B minor pentatonic positions
Develop wide vibrato technique in the Iommi style
Master bending accuracy and expressive phrasing
Combine all sections for a complete performance including tempo transitions

commonMistakes: Losing the power chord shape during slides between positions
Playing the intro too fast - it should be deliberately slow and heavy
Not adding enough palm muting, resulting in a muddy rather than chunky sound
Rushing the G5-F#5 oscillation instead of keeping it locked to the groove
Neglecting the tempo transition between the slow intro and fast main section
practiceRoutine: Warm up with slow power chord slides between B5, D5, and E5 for 5 minutes
Practice the main riff at 100 BPM with metronome for 10 minutes
Work on the G5-F#5 oscillation separately until it grooves naturally
Practice palm muting technique on a single chord at various pressures
Play the complete song structure at a comfortable tempo, building speed gradually
focusAreas: Clean power chord voicing maintained during sliding transitions
Consistent palm muting pressure for the thick, chugging sound
Accurate tempo management across the intro-to-verse speed transition
The rhythmic feel of the G5-F#5 oscillating riff section
Wide vibrato technique for the guitar solo
metronomeWork: Practice the slow intro at 76 BPM with quarter-note clicks
Work the main riff starting at 100 BPM, adding 10 BPM per session
Practice the tempo transition from 76 BPM intro to 164 BPM main riff
Use eighth-note subdivision clicks for the G5-F#5 oscillation precision
Target full song at 164 BPM with clean slides and consistent muting
